title: Pausing a city, or deleting a pincode from its coverage, does not stop serviceability or fulfilment - the fulfilment path never reads city_launch_configs
actor: Two actors, both authenticated. (1) Staff: app_users row USR-F38 / ops-f38@pawspace.test, role_code 'founder', holding launch.manage, authenticated by the forwarded-identity headers oai-authenticated-user-email + oai-authenticated-user-full-name(-encoding). (2) Customer: CUST-F38, a real platform session cookie issued via upsertIdentityBinding(customer_otp, verified) + issuePlatformSession, i.e. exactly the customer path. Non-preview (PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV=sandbox).
request: Sequence against the REAL exported handlers. (a) POST /api/uat-scheduling {clientRequestId:'GRP-F38-LIVE',customerId:'CUST-F38',petIds:['PET-F38'],serviceCode:'grooming',cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',scheduledStart:'2026-09-10T04:30:00.000Z',scheduledEnd:'2026-09-10T06:30:00.000Z'} with the customer cookie. (b) GET /api/city-governance as staff, then POST /api/city-governance {action:'save_city',city:{...the returned blr config...,status:'Paused'}} as staff - the real pause control surface. (c) POST /api/uat-scheduling with the same shape, clientRequestId 'GRP-F38-PAUSED', scheduledStart '2026-09-11T04:30:00.000Z'. (d) POST /api/canonical-bookings {idempotencyKey:'GRP-F38-PAUSED',scheduleGroupId:'GRP-F38-PAUSED',customer:{id:'CUST-F38',...},pets:[{sourceId:'PET-F38',...vaccinationStatus:'vaccinated'}],cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',serviceCode:'grooming',packageCode:'dog-basic',scheduledStart/End as (c),provider:<groom_arun as returned>,totalAmount:1899,amountDueNow:1899,payment:{method:'upi',mode:'prepaid',status:'created'},pricing:{discount:0}} with the customer cookie. (e) POST /api/city-governance {action:'save_city',city:{...,status:'Live',pincodes:'560001,560002,560003'}} - 560016 deleted from coverage. (f) POST /api/uat-scheduling clientRequestId 'GRP-F38-NOPIN', scheduledStart '2026-09-12T04:30:00.000Z', same blr/blr-east. (g) POST /api/grooming-service-location {bookingId:<the booking from (d)>,customerId:'CUST-F38',address:'F38 address',pincode:'560016',latitude:12.99,longitude:77.65} with the customer cookie.
response: (a) 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider.id:'groom_arun'}}. (b) 201 {data:{status:'Paused',version:2}} - the pause is accepted and persisted. (c) 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider.id:'groom_arun'}} - IDENTICAL to the pre-pause reserve. (d) 201 {data:{bookingId:'PS-UAT-MT87TK21-6AF8'}} - a confirmed booking in a paused city. (e) 201 {data:{status:'Live',pincodes:'560001,560002,560003'}}. (f) 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider.id:'groom_arun'}} - reserve for a pincode that is no longer in coverage. (g) 201 {data:{bookingId:'PS-UAT-MT87TK21-6AF8',addressSaved:true,coordinatesSaved:true,cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',navigationUrl:'https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=F38+address%2C+Ramamurthy+Nagar%2C+Bengaluru+560016&travelmode=driving'}} - the platform hands the groomer turn-by-turn directions to a pincode it no longer serves. Control side-by-side, same D1, same moment: lib/city-governance.ts resolveCityServiceCoverage(db,{cityCode:'blr',serviceCode:'grooming',pincode:'560016'}) returned {supported:true,reason:'live_and_explicitly_supported',startingPrice:1349} before the pause, {supported:false,reason:'city_not_live'} after the pause, and {supported:false,reason:'pincode_not_supported'} after the pincode deletion - while every fulfilment call above still returned 200/201.
d1_before: city_launch_configs: 1 row id='bengaluru', city_code='blr', status='Live', pincodes='560001,560002,560003,560005,560008,560016,...' , version=1. scheduling_reservations: empty. canonical_bookings: empty.
d1_after: city_launch_configs: id='bengaluru', city_code='blr', status='Live' (after step e), pincodes='560001,560002,560003' (560016 gone), version=3 - i.e. the governance table faithfully recorded both the pause and the coverage deletion. scheduling_reservations: 3 rows, group_id GRP-F38-LIVE / GRP-F38-PAUSED / GRP-F38-NOPIN, all provider_id='groom_arun', city_id='blr', status='assigned' - the paused-city and out-of-coverage reservations sit in the table indistinguishable from the legitimate one. canonical_bookings: 1 row id='PS-UAT-MT87TK21-6AF8', city_id='blr', service_code='grooming', status='confirmed'. booking_service_locations carries pincode 560016.
canonical_failure: city_launch_configs is a write-only governance record: pausing Bengaluru through POST /api/city-governance and then deleting 560016 from its coverage both persist (version 1 -> 3) and both are correctly reflected by lib/city-governance.ts resolveCityServiceCoverage, but that function has NO production caller - grep across app/, lib/, worker/ and backend/ finds it referenced only from tests/uat-closure-cross-module-governance.test.mjs - so the reserve path (app/api/uat-scheduling POST -> loadGovernedProviders, which filters provider_capacity_profiles by city_id/zones/live/status only), the booking path (app/api/canonical-bookings POST) and the service-location path (app/api/grooming-service-location POST -> lib/service-zones resolveZoneByPincode, which reads the hardcoded PINCODE_ZONE_MAP and service_zone_mappings) never consult it, so a customer session books, pays for and receives directions into a paused city and a deleted pincode exactly as before.
blast_radius: Every city-level and pincode-level kill switch the business has. Pause is the only lever Ops has to stop taking orders in a city (weather, a legal problem, no supply, a pilot being wound down) and it is inert against the money path; deleting a pincode is the only lever for shrinking a service area and it is equally inert. Both surfaces report success, increment a version, and write a security_audit_events row, so Ops has positive confirmation that a city is closed while customers keep transacting in it and providers keep being dispatched to it. Any city, any pincode, any of the five services; the ONLY reader that honours the setting is a function nothing calls.

title: Travel buffer and max-daily-jobs are enforced only in application code; the atomic reservation guard checks raw overlap alone
actor: Customer CUST-F30 holding a real platform session cookie (upsertIdentityBinding customer_otp verified -> issuePlatformSession), i.e. scheduling.book + ownership of its own customerId. A staff actor (app_users USR-P1 / ops-p1@pawspace.test, role_code 'founder', forwarded-identity headers, scheduling.manage) was used ONLY to set the stage through the real control surface: PATCH /api/provider-capacity-control to take groom_kiran and groom_sanjay live=0 so every request had to land on groom_arun, and to set groom_arun max_daily_jobs=2. The over-capacity writes themselves are made by the customer session. Non-preview (PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV=sandbox).
request: All calls POST /api/uat-scheduling (the real exported handler) with the customer cookie, payload {clientRequestId:<gid>,customerId:'CUST-F30',petIds:['PET-F30'],serviceCode:'grooming',cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',scheduledStart,scheduledEnd}. CONTROLS, issued sequentially: GRP-A1 2026-09-15T04:30Z-06:30Z then GRP-A2 2026-09-15T06:30Z-08:30Z (back-to-back, zero gap, groom_arun travel_buffer_minutes=30). GRP-C1 2026-09-17T03:30Z-05:30Z, GRP-C2 06:00Z-08:00Z, GRP-C3 08:30Z-10:30Z with max_daily_jobs=2. RACES, interleaved deterministically by holding request 1 at the instant it is about to run its guarded INSERT batch and running request 2 end-to-end in that window (the exact window the INSERT..SELECT..WHERE guard exists to close): (i) GRP-F1 2026-09-19T04:30Z-06:30Z held while GRP-F2 2026-09-19T06:30Z-08:30Z ran to completion; (ii) GRP-G1 2026-09-20T03:30Z-05:30Z committed first, then GRP-G2 06:00Z-08:00Z held while GRP-G3 08:30Z-10:30Z ran to completion.
response: CONTROLS - application code enforces both rules exactly as designed: GRP-A2 -> 409 {error:'NO_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE'} with evaluation reason 'Existing booking conflicts with travel/service buffer'; GRP-C3 -> 409 {error:'NO_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE'} with reason 'Daily job limit 2 reached'. RACES - both members of each race returned 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider:{id:'groom_arun'}}}: GRP-F1 200 and GRP-F2 200; GRP-G2 200 and GRP-G3 200. No 409, no SLOT_TAKEN, no rollback.
d1_before: provider_capacity_profiles groom_arun: live=1, status='active', capacity=1, travel_buffer_minutes=30, max_daily_jobs=4 (then 2 after the staff PATCH, response 200 {max_daily_jobs:2}); groom_kiran and groom_sanjay live=0. scheduling_reservations: no rows for 2026-09-19 or 2026-09-20.
d1_after: 2026-09-19: two rows, GRP-F1 04:30Z-06:30Z and GRP-F2 06:30Z-08:30Z, both provider_id='groom_arun', status='assigned' - measured gap between consecutive jobs 0 minutes against a configured travel_buffer_minutes of 30. 2026-09-20: three rows, GRP-G1 03:30Z-05:30Z, GRP-G2 06:00Z-08:00Z, GRP-G3 08:30Z-10:30Z, all provider_id='groom_arun', status='assigned' - 3 jobs on a day whose configured max_daily_jobs is 2 (gaps 30 and 30 minutes, i.e. exactly at the buffer, so only the daily limit is breached in that case and only the buffer in the other).
canonical_failure: The travel buffer and the daily job limit live only in backend/src/scheduling.ts evaluateProvider, which reads a snapshot of scheduling_reservations before the decision; the atomic guard in app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts insertReservations is 'INSERT INTO scheduling_reservations (...) SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scheduling_reservations WHERE provider_id=? AND status!="cancelled" AND scheduled_start<? AND scheduled_end>?)' - raw interval overlap on that provider and nothing else, with no buffer term and no per-day count - so two reservations that application code refuses individually both commit when they are interleaved, giving groom_arun back-to-back jobs with a 0-minute gap against a 30-minute configured buffer and 3 jobs against a configured limit of 2.
blast_radius: Every non-overnight service (grooming, dog_training, pet_taxi, dog_walking) in every city, under any concurrent load - two customers booking the same groomer at the same moment, or a customer retrying while an Ops reassign is in flight. Consequence is a provider physically unable to reach the second job (zero travel time is not an accounting error, it is a missed appointment) and providers pushed past the daily limit the platform contracted with them. The overnight branch of the same function DOES carry its capacity term into SQL ('(SELECT COALESCE(SUM(capacity_units),0) ...)+?<=?'), which shows the pattern was understood and simply not applied to the buffer or the daily count. Note the 200 responses give the customer a confirmed provider, so the mis-scheduling is discovered on the day.

title: A reservation dated two days in the past is scheduled, confirmed and paid
actor: Customer CUST-F34, a real platform session cookie (upsertIdentityBinding customer_otp verified -> issuePlatformSession) - scheduling.book plus ownership of its own customerId, no staff role, for the reserve and the booking. The sandbox payment legs additionally required a staff actor (app_users USR-P1 / ops-p1@pawspace.test, founder, forwarded-identity headers); called anonymously they answer 401 'Authentication required'. Non-preview (PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV=sandbox). Wall clock at execution: 2026-08-25T05:23Z.
request: (1) POST /api/uat-scheduling with the customer cookie: {clientRequestId:'GRP-F34-PAST',customerId:'CUST-F34',petIds:['PET-F34'],serviceCode:'grooming',cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',scheduledStart:'2026-08-23T04:30:00.000Z',scheduledEnd:'2026-08-23T06:30:00.000Z'} - two days before now, at 10:00-12:00 IST so it falls inside the roster window. (2) POST /api/canonical-bookings with the customer cookie: {idempotencyKey:'GRP-F34-PAST',scheduleGroupId:'GRP-F34-PAST',customer:{id:'CUST-F34',...},pets:[{sourceId:'PET-F34',...vaccinationStatus:'vaccinated'}],cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',serviceCode:'grooming',packageCode:'dog-basic',scheduledStart/End as above,provider:<groom_arun>,totalAmount:1899,amountDueNow:1899,payment:{method:'upi',mode:'prepaid',status:'created'},pricing:{discount:0}}. (3) POST /api/grooming-payment-sandbox {action:'link_order',bookingId,gatewayOrderId:'order_F34'} and {action:'simulate_event',bookingId,eventType:'payment.captured',eventId:'evt_F34',gatewayPaymentId:'pay_F34',amount:1899,currency:'INR'} as staff.
response: (1) 200 {data:{groupId:'GRP-F34-PAST',status:'assigned',provider:{id:'groom_arun',...}}} - no evaluation reason mentions the date. (2) 201 {data:{bookingId:'PS-UAT-MT87YW1Z-0E88'}}. (3) 201 and 201 {data:{eventType:'payment.captured',result:{duplicate:false,status:'processed',paymentId:'PAY-02CC1526'},environment:'sandbox',synthetic:true}}. Not one of the five calls mentions the date being in the past.
d1_before: scheduling_reservations, canonical_bookings, booking_payments, provider_work_orders: all empty for this group.
d1_after: scheduling_reservations: group_id='GRP-F34-PAST', provider_id='groom_arun', scheduled_start='2026-08-23T04:30:00.000Z', scheduled_end='2026-08-23T06:30:00.000Z', status='assigned', created_at=1787635412xxx (i.e. created two days AFTER the appointment it books). canonical_bookings: id='PS-UAT-MT87YW1Z-0E88', status='confirmed', scheduled_start='2026-08-23T04:30:00.000Z', total_amount=1899. booking_payments: id='PAY-02CC1526', status='captured', amount=1899, gateway='razorpay_sandbox'. provider_work_orders: booking_id='PS-UAT-MT87YW1Z-0E88', provider_id='groom_arun', status='assigned' - a live job dispatched into the past.
canonical_failure: Neither app/api/uat-scheduling POST nor backend/src/scheduling.ts buildOccurrences/evaluateProvider nor app/api/canonical-bookings POST compares scheduledStart to now, so a customer session reserves, confirms and pays 1899 for a grooming appointment dated 2026-08-23 while the clock reads 2026-08-25, ending with a confirmed booking, a captured payment and an assigned provider work order for a slot that has already passed.
blast_radius: Every service and every city. A past-dated slot can never be delivered, so the row is guaranteed to become a refund, a dispute or a false no-show against the provider; it also silently consumes that provider's overlap guard and daily count for a day that is already over, and it lands in the day board and in revenue as a confirmed, paid booking. It needs no privilege beyond an ordinary logged-in customer, and because the only bound on scheduledStart is the roster window (09:00-19:00 IST for grooming) any past date works, not just recent ones. Same absence lets a booking be dated arbitrarily far in the future.

title: A provider's max_daily_jobs of 0 is read back as 6, giving them MORE work than their configured limit of 4
actor: Staff for the configuration write: app_users USR-P1 / ops-p1@pawspace.test, role_code 'founder', holding scheduling.manage, authenticated by the forwarded-identity headers (oai-authenticated-user-email + oai-authenticated-user-full-name + -encoding). Customer CUST-F29 with a real platform session cookie (customer_otp verified -> issuePlatformSession) for the reserves that consume the capacity. Non-preview (PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV=sandbox).
request: (1) PATCH /api/provider-capacity-control {providerId:'taxi_rahul',changes:{max_daily_jobs:0},reason:'stand this driver down, no jobs today'} as staff. taxi_meera and taxi_imran were first set live:0 by the same route so every request had to land on taxi_rahul. (2) lib/provider-capacity-governance.ts getGovernedProvider(db,'taxi_rahul') and loadGovernedProviders(db,'blr','blr-east','pet_taxi'). (3) eight sequential POST /api/uat-scheduling reserves as the customer, serviceCode 'pet_taxi' (45-minute service, 20-minute buffer, roster 06:00-22:00 IST), 2026-09-22, slots every 65 minutes from 00:30Z. (4) then PATCH the same provider to {max_daily_jobs:4} and repeat six reserves on 2026-09-23. (5) corollary: PATCH {providerId:'taxi_imran',changes:{capacity:0,travel_buffer_minutes:0,max_daily_jobs:0}}.
response: (1) 200 {data:{max_daily_jobs:0,version:2}} - the PATCH accepts 0 without comment (its only numeric check is Number(value)<0). (2) getGovernedProvider -> {maxDailyJobs:6, capacity:1, travelBufferMinutes:20, live:true}; loadGovernedProviders -> [{id:'taxi_rahul',maxDailyJobs:6}]. (3) reserves 1-6 all 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider:{id:'taxi_rahul'}}}; reserves 7 and 8 -> 409 {error:'NO_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE'} with the evaluation reason 'Daily job limit 6 reached' - the engine states the number 6 out loud for a provider whose row says 0. (4) 200 {max_daily_jobs:4}, readback maxDailyJobs=4, and exactly four reserves accepted, the fifth refused 'Daily job limit 4 reached'. (5) 200; readback {capacity:1, travelBufferMinutes:30, maxDailyJobs:6} for a row that literally reads 0,0,0.
d1_before: provider_capacity_profiles taxi_rahul: max_daily_jobs=8 (integer), capacity=1, travel_buffer_minutes=20, live=1, version=1, updated_by='founder_seed'. No reservations on 2026-09-22.
d1_after: provider_capacity_profiles taxi_rahul: max_daily_jobs=0, typeof(max_daily_jobs)='integer', version=2, updated_by='ops-p1@pawspace.test' - the 0 is stored correctly and durably. scheduling_reservations: SIX rows for 2026-09-22, GRP-TAXI-0..GRP-TAXI-5, all provider_id='taxi_rahul', status='assigned', against a stored limit of 0. On 2026-09-23 with the limit at 4, exactly four rows - correct. taxi_imran after the corollary PATCH: capacity=0, travel_buffer_minutes=0, max_daily_jobs=0 stored, read back as 1, 30 and 6.
canonical_failure: lib/provider-capacity-governance.ts rowToProvider builds every numeric field with a JavaScript ||-fallback - maxDailyJobs:Number(row.max_daily_jobs||6), capacity:Number(row.capacity||1), travelBufferMinutes:Number(row.travel_buffer_minutes||30) - so the one value an operator uses to stand a provider down, 0, is falsy and is silently replaced by the hardcoded default, and a driver whose D1 row says max_daily_jobs=0 is given six jobs by the scheduler, which then refuses the seventh with 'Daily job limit 6 reached'.
refutation: HALF THE TITLE IS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. There is no defect at 4: a provider PATCHed to max_daily_jobs=4 reads back as 4 and receives exactly four jobs, the fifth refused 'Daily job limit 4 reached' - executed and confirmed. The defect is specific to 0 (and to any falsy value). The '4' in the frozen title is the seeded limit that groom_arun/groom_sanjay carry, and the true statement is that a provider stood down to 0 gets SIX jobs - more than the four the default roster gives an ordinary grooming provider - not that a provider configured for 4 gets more than 4.
blast_radius: Every provider in every city and every service. 0 is the natural way for Ops to express 'no work for this provider' - a suspension, a sick day, a driver whose licence is being re-checked, a host being wound down - and the PATCH accepts it, stores it, versions it, writes a provider_capacity_audit row and a security_audit_events row, and the capacity-control GET shows 0 back to the operator, while the scheduler hands the provider six jobs a day. Same idiom silently rewrites capacity 0 to 1 (a boarding host with zero kennels still takes a stay) and travel_buffer_minutes 0 to 30. It fails OPEN: the control permits exactly what it was set to refuse. Only staff holding scheduling.manage can set it, but the resulting over-assignment is then driven by ordinary customer sessions.

title: Non-numeric capacity accepted by the capacity-control PATCH makes a provider permanently unbookable behind a false 'SLOT_TAKEN' message
risk_category: fail-open policy enforcement (at the config gate) with fail-closed fulfilment (at the booking gate)
actor: Staff for the configuration write: app_users USR-P1 / ops-p1@pawspace.test, role_code 'founder', scheduling.manage, forwarded-identity headers. Customer CUST-F29 with a real platform session cookie for the boarding reserves. Non-preview (PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV=sandbox).
request: (1) Baseline: POST /api/uat-scheduling as the customer {clientRequestId:'GRP-BOARD-OK',customerId:'CUST-F29',petIds:['PET-BOARD'],serviceCode:'boarding',cityId:'blr',zoneId:'blr-east',preferredProviderId:'host_maya_rohan',careMode:'overnight',scheduledStart:'2026-09-25T04:30:00.000Z',scheduledEnd:'2026-09-27T04:30:00.000Z'} (canonical_pets row PET-BOARD owned by CUST-F29 with vaccination_status='verified'). (2) PATCH /api/provider-capacity-control {providerId:'host_maya_rohan',changes:{capacity:'four'},reason:'typo in the capacity field'} as staff. (3) GET /api/provider-capacity-control?cityId=blr&service=boarding as staff. (4) the same boarding reserve twice more, clientRequestId 'GRP-BOARD-BAD-1' and 'GRP-BOARD-BAD-2'. (5) the same reserve against a different host, preferredProviderId:'host_sana'. Corollary: PATCH {providerId:'taxi_meera',changes:{max_daily_jobs:'none',travel_buffer_minutes:'none'}}.
response: (1) 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider:{id:'host_maya_rohan'}}}. (2) 200 {data:{capacity:'four',version:2}} - the string is accepted with no error, because the PATCH's only numeric check is `Number(value)<0` and Number('four') is NaN, which is not < 0. (3) 200, profiles show host_maya_rohan capacity:'four' - the operator is shown the typo but never told it is invalid. (4) BOTH attempts 409 {error:'SLOT_TAKEN', message:'Another reservation took this provider/slot a moment ago - pick a different time or retry for the next eligible provider'} - a message that names a concurrent booker who does not exist. (5) 200 {data:{status:'assigned',provider:{id:'host_sana'}}} - so it is this host and only this host that is dead. Corollary PATCH: 200, readback {travelBufferMinutes:NaN, maxDailyJobs:NaN}.
d1_before: provider_capacity_profiles host_maya_rohan: capacity=4, typeof(capacity)='integer', max_daily_jobs=12, live=1, status='active', version=1. scheduling_reservations: one row, GRP-BOARD-OK, provider_id='host_maya_rohan', status='assigned' - the baseline stay, leaving 3 of 4 kennel units free.
d1_after: provider_capacity_profiles host_maya_rohan: capacity='four', typeof(capacity)='text', version=2, updated_by='ops-p1@pawspace.test'; a provider_capacity_audit row and a security_audit_events row both record the change as a completed success. scheduling_reservations for this host: STILL exactly the one baseline row - neither failed attempt left anything behind, so there was never a competing reservation for the 'SLOT_TAKEN' message to refer to. lib/provider-capacity-governance.ts getGovernedProvider(db,'host_maya_rohan') returns capacity=NaN, live=true.
canonical_failure: The capacity-control PATCH validates numbers only with `Number(value)<0`, which NaN fails to trip, so the string 'four' is written into provider_capacity_profiles.capacity as TEXT; rowToProvider then yields capacity=NaN, the application-level overnight check `used+petIds.length>(provider.capacity??1)` is false for NaN so the provider stays eligible and is selected, and the atomic guard `... (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(capacity_units),0) ... )+?<=?` binds NaN so the INSERT..SELECT matches zero rows and the route raises SlotConflictError - the customer is told twice, deterministically, that 'another reservation took this provider/slot a moment ago' when the host is simply permanently unbookable.
blast_radius: One typo in an Ops capacity field silently removes a boarding host from the platform for as long as nobody notices. The failure is invisible from every angle Ops has: the PATCH returned 200, the audit trail records a completed change, and the capacity-control GET renders 'four' as if it were a value. The customer-facing symptom is a lie that invites a retry ('pick a different time or retry'), so the host looks fully booked rather than misconfigured, and every retry reproduces it. Note the two halves fail in OPPOSITE directions: the configuration gate fails OPEN (it accepts a value it should reject and records success), while fulfilment then fails CLOSED (it refuses bookings it should accept) - which is why the finding is a revenue and supply loss rather than an over-booking. The same non-numeric write on max_daily_jobs and travel_buffer_minutes is equally accepted and reads back NaN, where NaN comparisons make the daily limit and the travel buffer unenforceable instead - that direction is fail-open, and was confirmed at the readback level, not driven to a booking.
